discovery-weak-signals.name: AI/HPC demand durability
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Primary monthly revenue and Q2 management commentary show strong leading-edge demand and a raised 2026 growth/capex posture.

discovery-weak-signals.name: Manufacturing bottleneck power
discovery-weak-signals.basis: The capex mix concentrates on advanced process and packaging, reinforcing TSMC's position at multiple constrained layers of AI compute supply.

discovery-weak-signals.name: Geographic resilience
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Arizona scale adds geographic manufacturing and packaging redundancy, while overseas fabs carry explicit margin dilution and execution complexity.

discovery-weak-signals.name: 2nm transition
discovery-weak-signals.basis: 2nm already represented 3% of Q2 wafer revenue and is entering a steep ramp, but management expects 3-4 percentage points of gross-margin dilution from the ramp in 2H26.

expectations-execution.name: Execution versus narrative
expectations-execution.basis: Revenue, earnings, advanced-node mix and capacity construction provide primary evidence that leading-edge demand is converting into operating results and physical capacity.

expectations-execution.name: Expectation burden
expectations-execution.basis: Raised growth and capex expectations increase the amount of future utilization, yield and margin execution required to justify the expansion.

expectations-execution.name: Margin resilience
expectations-execution.basis: Q2 gross margin was 67.7%, but management explicitly forecasts 2nm and overseas-fab dilution during the coming ramp.

expectations-execution.name: Capital intensity
expectations-execution.basis: US$60-64B of 2026 capex supports future bottleneck capacity but raises execution and return-on-capital requirements.

riskEvidence.basis: Leadership/liquidity offset geopolitical, geographic, cyclicality, capex and concentration risk.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current issuer operating/governance evidence plus current external valuation evidence; residual concentration/geopolitical unknowns preserved.

scoreRecord.thesis: TSMC combines exceptional realized financial momentum with dominant control of leading-edge fabrication bottlenecks and a steep 2nm ramp, making it foundational to 2036 compute infrastructure; geopolitical concentration is the principal structural counterweight.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A Taiwan geopolitical disruption, geographic manufacturing concentration, customer/platform concentration or successful foundry substitution could impair a business whose valuation now reflects substantial continued leadership.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 results and 2nm ramp evidence against management's $44.6B-$45.8B revenue and 65%-67% gross-margin guidance.

items.risk: Management expects the steep 2nm ramp to dilute gross margin by about 3-4 percentage points in 2H26.
Overseas-fab expansion is expected to dilute gross margin by 2-3% in early stages and 3-4% later, creating a real cost of geographic diversification.
Consumer and price-sensitive end markets remain challenged by component prices and macro uncertainty even while AI demand is robust.
Security-level valuation attractiveness is not asserted because no canonical live valuation/entry input was part of this work item; this is non-gating.
A high expectation base creates downside sensitivity if AI demand, 2nm yields, packaging throughput or overseas-fab ramps disappoint.
Geopolitical concentration remains material despite geographic expansion because the most advanced capacity and ecosystem cannot be replicated instantly.
Geopolitical Taiwan concentration remains a structural tail risk even as overseas capacity expands.
Very high capex and overseas expansion can pressure returns if demand utilization normalizes sharply.
Large forward capex raises downside sensitivity to utilization and pricing.
Taiwan concentration remains a low-frequency/high-severity operational risk.
Issuer-origin materials dominate operating and technology evidence; external market data independently addresses valuation but not competitive claims.
Taiwan geopolitical/geographic concentration is the dominant tail risk despite global expansion and liquidity.
Leading-edge capex intensity and customer concentration can amplify cyclical or platform-specific shocks.
